subject: Throughput benchmarking & SLA measurement — Dedicated GPU pool request
messages:
From: Sophie Lang <sophie.lang@nimbushealth.com>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.example>
Date: Fri, 1 Jun 2028 09:22:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated throughput guarantee ask and pricing / sizing worksheet

Hi Mateo,

Quick note to surface Nimbus Health's initial throughput ask for our Dedicated GPU pool evaluation. We're preparing a procurement request and need firm guidance so we can align finance and infra. High level:

- Target sustained throughput: 100,000 tokens/sec for our baseline model (mix of chat & gen traffic)
- P95 latency target: <200ms for a 32-token generation
- Expected concurrency: ~220 concurrent sessions with session-level KV cache used
- Preferred term: 12-month reserved commit; looking for a discount ~35% off list if the above can be contractually guaranteed

Can you provide:
- Measurement methodology (how you measure tokens/sec vs requests/sec, acceptable test harness, windowing)
- A draft SLA and how credits are calculated if SLOs aren't met
- Initial sizing estimate (GPUs/pool) and whether Redwood needs any sampling hooks/telemetry from our side

I've attached our SizingTemplate with our peak distributions and some sample prompt mixes. Sophie

[Attachment: Nimbus_SizingTemplate.xlsx (xlsx, 48KB)]

From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.example>
To: Sophie Lang <sophie.lang@nimbushealth.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.example>
Date: Fri, 1 Jun 2028 11:01:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated throughput guarantee ask and pricing / sizing worksheet

Hi Sophie — thanks for the clear ask and for sending the sizing sheet. Quick summary up front, then a proposed measurement and commercial approach.

Short answer on guarantees: we can offer a contract-backed throughput guarantee, but we split the guarantee into two pieces to align engineering reality with commercial certainty. Proposal:

- Rate floor (sustained): 80k tokens/sec sustained, measured across a 30-minute acceptance window (see method below).
- Burst window: up to 130k tokens/sec for bursts up to 10 minutes (no credits for transient bursts).
- Latency SLOs tied to canonical prompt shape: P95 < 220ms for 32-token generation; P99 < 350ms.
- Commercial ask: 12-month reservation -> 28% discount off hosted list; 24-month -> 32%. We can discuss a one-time promotional credit to approximate the 35% you asked for if you commit to a usage ramp schedule.

Why the split: raw tokens/sec guarantees are heavily sensitive to prompt length distribution, KV cache hit rates, and model config (quantization, beam size). For contractual clarity we use a canonical test harness with a reproducible prompt mix (you provided a good start).

Measurement methodology (proposed acceptance test):
- Tooling: Redwood throughput-harness v2 (we'll run in your VPC or a redwood-managed test tenant).
- Workload shape: use your provided distribution (we request the anonymized percentile list you attached) + an agreed standard mix: 60% short (<=32 tokens), 20% mid (64 tokens), 20% long tail (>=256 tokens).
- Warmup: 10 minute warmup to populate KV cache; cold-start behavior measured separately and excluded from sustained window.
- Sustained window: 30-minute measurement window; compute a 5-minute sliding average and take the median of those averages as the sustained tokens/sec value. Acceptance requires median sliding average >= rate floor.
- Latency: measure P95 and P99 on individual request completion times for the canonical 32-token prompt case during the same sustained window.
- Concurrency measurement: record requests/sec and backpressure events; if queueing > 2% of requests we consider the run failed.
- Runs: 3 accepted runs within a 5-day test window; at least 2 runs must pass to accept production SLA.

SLA credits (draft):
- If monthly sustained tokens/sec (as measured by auto-sampling in production) falls below contracted floor for more than two contiguous 6-hour windows, customer receives a service credit equal to 2% of monthly invoice per 1% shortfall, capped at 20%.
- Latency misses are measured separately and yield credits on a tiered scale (detailed in attached SLA draft).

Sizing notes (quick):
- Based on the prompt mixes you shared and our typical model footprints, the baseline pool to target the 80k sustained + 130k burst is ~6x A100-80GB-equivalent GPUs (with continuous batching and kernel selection optimizations). If you want 100k sustained reliably, that's closer to 8–9 GPUs.
- We recommend a +20% headroom for business hours head spikes and autoscaling burst capacity (separate burst billing).

Next steps:
1) If you agree to the measurement method, we'll schedule the acceptance runs and I'll attach a draft SLA + sizing workbook.
2) If you want us to run the benchmark inside your VPC, we'll send an onboarding checklist and a short telemetry addon to capture request-level traces (read-only).

I've attached a short SLA draft and a Redwood-runner checklist. Happy to join a call with Tom/Sophie to walk the test plan.

Best,
Mateo
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: Redwood_SLA_Draft.pdf (pdf, 22KB)]

From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.example>
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.example>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.example>
Date: Fri, 1 Jun 2028 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Dedicated throughput guarantee ask — internal recommendation

Laura/Ben — looped you in for pricing/ops runbook approval. Client (Nimbus) asked for 100k sustained + P95 <200ms; I proposed a conservative commercial floor (80k sustained / 130k burst / P95 220ms) with 28% for 12 months.

Recommendation for negotiation leverage:
- Offer: 12-mo reserved commit with 28% discount + one-time onboarding credit (equivalent to additional ~3% discount) if they sign within 30 days. Require a 2-week acceptance test window and a rolling 30-day ramp for usage-based overages during the first 60 days.
- Approvals needed: 28% is within standard delegated authority; any move to 32–35% needs manager sign-off and finance sign-off on revenue recognition (Ben).
- Ops ask: require Redwood Ops engineer on the acceptance test day and agree to a single tenant-run (their model) benchmark; if their model shows higher footprint we can request a bump in committed GPUs or a phased commit increase.

Please confirm if we can proceed with the 28% + onboarding credit, and I'll lock the test dates.

—Mateo

From: Tom Rivera <tom.rivera@nimbushealth.com>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.example>
Cc: Sophie Lang <sophie.lang@nimbushealth.com>
Date: Sat, 2 Jun 2028 08:43:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated throughput guarantee ask and pricing / sizing worksheet

Thanks Mateo — this is helpful. A few clarifications before we proceed:

- Measurement shape: we insist that tokens/sec be measured against a realistic prompt distribution (our production 50th/90th/99th percentiles are in the attached sheet). In particular, our environment has a heavier long-tail — about 20% of requests go >512 tokens. Please include an explicit long-tail run in the acceptance test and show per-percentile breakdowns.
- Cold starts: we want the first 100 requests (cold cache) included as a separate cold-start SLA evaluation. We understand bursts may be excluded, but cold-start latency impacts UX and needs visibility.
- Benchmark on our tenant: we will provide a sanitized model snapshot and a sample production trace for Redwood to run the benchmark in our VPC. This needs to be scheduled the week of June 12.
- Contract: we will want the measurement method written into the SOW (acceptance criteria + test harness version). Can you provide reproducible scripts and the harness container image id?

If you can agree to include the long-tail percentile reporting and a cold-start evaluation, I'm comfortable moving to a 12-month commit at the discount levels you're proposing, pending final legal review.

Tom
Director of Infra Engineering, Nimbus Health
[Attachment: nimbus_percentiles.csv (csv, 18KB)]

From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.example>
To: Tom Rivera <tom.rivera@nimbushealth.com>, Sophie Lang <sophie.lang@nimbushealth.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.example>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.example>
Date: Sat, 2 Jun 2028 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated throughput guarantee ask and pricing / sizing worksheet — next steps

Tom/Sophie — great feedback, agree on including the long-tail percentile reporting and a separate cold-start evaluation. Action items / timeline:

1) We'll publish the throughput-harness v2 container id and the reproducible test scripts to the shared Drive by Monday. Link will be in the SOW.
2) Proposed acceptance window: week of June 12 (two candidate days: June 13 or 15). Redwood Ops will be on the call to run the tenant benchmark inside your VPC using the sanitized snapshot.
3) Contract language: we'll add the exact measurement steps (warmup, sliding-window median, percentile reporting) into the SOW and attach the harness repo + container id.
4) Commercial: confirm 12-month at 28% + onboarding credit (3%) pending successful acceptance runs; we'll generate the preliminary order form and HubSpot record (https://hubspot.example/deal/7421).

I'll prepare the SOW addendum and SLA clause and circulate for signature. Let me know which day you prefer for the test and whether Redwood should pull telemetry (read-only) from your staging cluster.

—Mateo
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
[Related: https://hubspot.example/deal/7421]
